QUESTION: To identify molecular subtypes of NAFLD for clinical-trial enrichment, can unsupervised clustering of hepatic transcriptomes stratify patients by disease severity?

ANSWER: No — standard unsupervised hierarchical clustering on the dominant transcriptomic axes does NOT stratify NAFLD patients by disease severity (fibrosis stage, NAS score, NASH group, or early/moderate stage).

ANALYSIS DETAILS AND EVIDENCE:

Cohort: GSE135251, 206 NAFLD patients (10 healthy controls excluded). Counts were VST-normalized and filtered to 16,549 expressed genes. PCA on the top 3,000 HVGs revealed that the dominant transcriptomic axis (PC1, 33.9% of variance) is uncorrelated with fibrosis stage (Spearman rho=-0.074, p=0.29) and NAS score (rho=0.072, p=0.30). PC1 is driven by metabolic/transport genes (ATP6V1A, GALNT1, TNPO1) reflecting basal hepatic biology rather than disease severity.

Hierarchical clustering (Ward linkage, 15 PCs, k=2 by silhouette optimization) yielded two clusters (n=52 and n=154) that showed no significant association with any clinical severity metric: fibrosis Kruskal-Wallis p=0.36, NAS p=0.16, paper group chi-square p=0.49, early/moderate Fisher exact p=0.61.

The clinical severity signal DOES exist but is concentrated in PC3 (7.5% variance), which strongly correlates with fibrosis (rho=0.655, p=1.4e-26) and NAS (rho=0.479, p=3.4e-13). PC3 is driven by a coherent fibrosis/stellate-cell activation/ECM-remodeling program including SOX9, THBS2, LUM, FAP, JAG1, CD24, EPCAM, and inflammatory chemokines. When clustering is restricted to clinically-correlated PCs (exploratory supervised approach), severity-stratified clusters emerge (fibrosis p=3.4e-4, NAS p=3.1e-7).

INTERPRETATION: The largest molecular variation among NAFLD hepatic transcriptomes reflects differences in basal hepatocyte biology (metabolic zonation, tissue composition) that are independent of standard histological grading. The fibrosis-driven severity program exists but constitutes a minority of the transcriptomic variance. For clinical-trial enrichment, a simple transcriptome-wide clustering approach would not yield severity-stratified subgroups. Alternative strategies — such as supervised classifiers trained on the known fibrosis/NAS-associated gene program, or using PC3 alone as a continuous molecular severity score — would be more effective.
